personality.meaning: The qualities and characteristics that make a person different from other people.
personality.example: Her warm personality made her popular with every new colleague.

influence.meaning: To affect how someone thinks, behaves or develops, or how something happens.
influence.example: Living abroad as a child strongly influenced his taste in food.

factor.meaning: One of several things that cause or affect a particular result or situation.
factor.example: Money was only one factor in her decision to move.

contribute to.meaning: To be one of the causes of something or help it to happen.
contribute to.example: Poor sleep can contribute to stress and bad moods.

achievement.meaning: Something important that you succeed in doing, usually through effort or skill.
achievement.example: Finishing a marathon at sixty was a remarkable achievement.

disappointment.meaning: A feeling of sadness because something was not as good as you hoped, or a thing that causes it.
disappointment.example: Losing the final was a bitter disappointment for the whole team.

first-born.meaning: Describes the child who was born before all the other children in a family.
first-born.example: As the first-born, she often had to look after her younger brothers.

ambitious.meaning: Having a strong wish to be successful, powerful or rich, and willing to work hard for it.
ambitious.example: He is an ambitious young lawyer who hopes to become a judge.

rebellious.meaning: Refusing to obey rules or accept authority, especially because you disagree with them.
rebellious.example: As a rebellious teenager, he refused to wear the school uniform.

argumentative.meaning: Often disagreeing or starting arguments with other people.
argumentative.example: My argumentative uncle turns every family dinner into a debate.

stubborn.meaning: Determined to do what you want and refusing to change your mind, even when others disagree.
stubborn.example: She was too stubborn to admit that she had taken the wrong road.

inherit.meaning: To receive a quality or characteristic from your parents through your genes.
inherit.example: I inherited my father's dark hair and his terrible sense of direction.

characteristic.meaning: A typical quality or feature that makes a person or thing recognisable.
characteristic.example: Honesty is the characteristic I admire most in a friend.

curious.meaning: Eager to learn or know about something or someone.
curious.example: The curious toddler opened every cupboard in the kitchen.

cheerful.meaning: Happy and positive in the way you behave and speak.
cheerful.example: The cheerful receptionist greeted every visitor with a big smile.

adventurous.meaning: Willing to try new, unusual or risky things.
adventurous.example: We are an adventurous family, so we camp somewhere different every summer.

outgoing.meaning: Friendly, energetic and enjoying meeting and talking to new people.
outgoing.example: Her outgoing nature helped her make friends quickly in the new city.

sociable.meaning: Enjoying spending time with other people and being friendly towards them.
sociable.example: He's very sociable and organises a party almost every month.

break the rules.meaning: To do something that is not allowed by an official or accepted set of instructions.
break the rules.example: Employees who break the rules may lose their jobs.

relaxed.meaning: Calm and not worried or nervous about anything.
relaxed.example: After the holiday he felt relaxed and ready to return to work.

optimistic.meaning: Expecting good things to happen and believing that situations will turn out well.
optimistic.example: I'm optimistic that we'll find a solution before the deadline.

pessimistic.meaning: Expecting bad things to happen and believing that situations will turn out badly.
pessimistic.example: Don't be so pessimistic; the interview might go very well.

realistic.meaning: Understanding what is actually possible and dealing with situations in a sensible way.
realistic.example: Be realistic: you can't learn fluent Japanese in three months.

generous.meaning: Willing to give more money, time or help than is expected.
generous.example: A generous donor paid for the new library.

reliable.meaning: Able to be trusted to do what you expect or say you will do.
reliable.example: She is a reliable colleague who always meets her deadlines.

thoughtful.meaning: Considerate and showing that you think about other people's feelings and needs.
thoughtful.example: It was thoughtful of you to bring soup when I was ill.

practical.meaning: Good at making sensible decisions and doing useful things rather than just thinking about them.
practical.example: My practical sister fixed the broken shelf in ten minutes.

musical.meaning: Good at or interested in playing, singing or understanding music.
musical.example: He comes from a musical family, and everyone plays an instrument.

emotional.meaning: Having strong feelings that you show openly, or relating to feelings.
emotional.example: She became emotional when she saw her old school again.

artistic.meaning: Having a natural skill for creating things such as paintings, designs or music.
artistic.example: My artistic cousin designs all the posters for the festival.

talented.meaning: Having a natural ability to do something well without being taught.
talented.example: The talented young pianist won a national competition.

hopeful.meaning: Feeling that something you want is likely to happen.
hopeful.example: We are hopeful that the weather will improve by the weekend.

identity.meaning: The qualities, beliefs and background that make a person or group different from others.
identity.example: Language is an important part of a nation's identity.

cultural heritage.meaning: The traditions, customs and history that a group or country has passed down over time.
cultural heritage.example: The festival celebrates the region's rich cultural heritage.

online persona.meaning: The image or character that a person presents to others on the internet.
online persona.example: His cheerful online persona hides how shy he really is.

physical appearance.meaning: The way a person's body and face look to other people.
physical appearance.example: Employers should not judge candidates by their physical appearance.

belonging.meaning: The feeling of being happy and accepted as part of a group or place.
belonging.example: Joining the choir gave him a real sense of belonging.

nationality.meaning: The legal status of belonging to a particular country.
nationality.example: She has dual nationality because her mother is Finnish and her father is Italian.

immigrant.meaning: A person who comes to live permanently in a country that is not their own.
immigrant.example: His grandparents were immigrants who opened a small bakery.

identify with.meaning: To feel that you share the same feelings, background or qualities as someone or something.
identify with.example: Many young readers identify with the main character of the novel.

settle for.meaning: To accept something that is less good than you really wanted.
settle for.example: I won't settle for a job that I don't enjoy.

award-winning.meaning: Having received a prize because of its high quality.
award-winning.example: The award-winning documentary changed how people think about plastic.

co-found.meaning: To start a company or organisation together with one or more other people.
co-found.example: She co-founded a software company with two university friends.

brand.meaning: A product, company or person's image and name that people recognise and associate with certain qualities.
brand.example: A strong personal brand can help you find freelance work.

represent.meaning: To show or express the qualities or ideas of a person, group or thing.
represent.example: The logo is designed to represent the company's friendly image.

attitude.meaning: The way you think and feel about something, which affects how you behave.
attitude.example: A positive attitude to mistakes helps you learn faster.

background.meaning: The details of a person's family, education, culture and experience.
background.example: The students come from very different cultural backgrounds.

romantic.meaning: Expressive of or connected with feelings of love, or having an idealistic and emotional view of life.
romantic.example: Italian sounds romantic to many people who don't speak it.

get the job done.example: She works quietly but always gets the job done.

lifestyle.meaning: The way a person or group lives, including their habits, work and free-time activities.
lifestyle.example: A healthy lifestyle includes regular exercise and enough sleep.

interact with.meaning: To communicate with or react to other people while spending time with them.
interact with.example: Children learn a lot by interacting with others of different ages.

survey.meaning: A set of questions asked to many people to find out their opinions or behaviour.
survey.example: A recent survey shows that most students prefer studying online.

paragliding.meaning: A sport in which you fly through the air using a large cloth wing after jumping from a high place.
paragliding.example: We tried paragliding over the Alps and it was unforgettable.

applicant.meaning: A person who formally asks for a job, place on a course or other opportunity.
applicant.example: There were over two hundred applicants for the position.

raise money.meaning: To collect money from people, usually for a charity or a particular purpose.
raise money.example: The students raised money for the hospital by running a marathon.

duration.meaning: The length of time that something continues or lasts.
duration.example: Passengers must keep their seat belts fastened for the duration of the flight.

emphasise.meaning: To show or say that something is especially important or deserves particular attention.
emphasise.example: The teacher emphasised the need to revise regularly.

unfinished.example: He left the painting unfinished when he moved abroad.

in progress.meaning: Happening now and not yet finished.
in progress.example: Please be quiet; an exam is in progress.

state verb.meaning: A verb that describes a condition or situation rather than an action, such as know or own.
state verb.example: State verbs like believe are not usually used in continuous tenses.

focus on.meaning: To give most of your attention to one particular thing.
focus on.example: This lesson focuses on the difference between two tenses.

weak form.meaning: The short, unstressed way a word is pronounced in normal connected speech.
weak form.example: The weak form of "have" is often hard to hear in fast speech.

strong form.meaning: The full, stressed way a word is pronounced, usually when said alone or for emphasis.
strong form.example: We use the strong form of "been" when we want to stress it.

pie chart.meaning: A circular diagram divided into sections to show how a whole is shared between parts.
pie chart.example: The pie chart shows how the company spends its budget.
